installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Bannerlord Coop dedicated server - installation script
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
# Image to install with is 'ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/installers:debian'
#
# The Coop dedicated server (BannerlordCoopServer.exe) ships INSIDE the mod's Steam
# Workshop item, which is published under the base game's App ID (261550) rather than
# as a free dedicated-server tool. The Steam account used must therefore OWN Mount &
# Blade II: Bannerlord - anonymous login cannot fetch it. The item also bundles the
# Bannerlord engine and a .NET runtime, so the free Dedicated Server tool (app
# 1863440) is NOT needed.
#
# WHY NOT SteamCMD: +workshop_download_item aborts on multi-GB workshop items with
# "ERROR! Timeout downloading item" or "(Failure)" and never finishes this one - a
# well-known SteamCMD limitation, reproduced here over 24 consecutive resume attempts.
# DepotDownloader (SteamRE, authors of SteamKit2) fetches the same UGC without it.

if [[ "${STEAM_USER}" == "" ]] || [[ "${STEAM_PASS}" == "" ]]; then
    echo "-----------------------------------------"
    echo "A Steam account that owns Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord is required to"
    echo "download the Coop Workshop item. Anonymous login will not work."
    echo "Set the Steam User / Steam Password variables and reinstall."
    echo "-----------------------------------------"
    exit 1
fi

apt -y update
apt -y --no-install-recommends install curl unzip ca-certificates

STAGING="/mnt/server/.ugc-staging"
DD_DIR="/mnt/server/.depotdownloader"
SENTINEL_REL="DedicatedServer/engine/bin/Win64_Shipping_Server/TaleWorlds.Starter.DotNetCore.dll"

## Staged inside /mnt/server rather than /tmp: the payload is several GB and counts
## against the server's disk quota either way, but /tmp is often far smaller.
rm -rf "${STAGING}" "${DD_DIR}"
mkdir -p "${STAGING}" "${DD_DIR}"

## Fetch DepotDownloader. The linux-x64 build is self-contained, so no system .NET
## runtime has to be installed into the image.
DD_VERSION="3.4.0"
DD_URL="https://github.com/SteamRE/DepotDownloader/releases/download/DepotDownloader_${DD_VERSION}/DepotDownloader-linux-x64.zip"

echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Fetching DepotDownloader ${DD_VERSION}..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"
cd "${DD_DIR}"
if ! curl -fsSL -o depotdownloader.zip "${DD_URL}"; then
    echo "Could not download DepotDownloader from ${DD_URL}"
    exit 1
fi
unzip -oq depotdownloader.zip -d "${DD_DIR}"
chmod +x "${DD_DIR}/DepotDownloader"

## Download the workshop item.
##
## -remember-password persists the Steam session, so the Steam Guard mobile
## confirmation is only needed on the first install for this account.
## -validate checksums anything already on disk, which makes a re-run resume rather
## than refetch.
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Downloading workshop item ${WORKSHOP_ITEM_ID} (several GB - this takes a while)."
echo "If the account has a Steam Guard mobile authenticator, CONFIRM THE LOGIN ON"
echo "YOUR PHONE now - the install waits here until you do."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

"${DD_DIR}/DepotDownloader" \
    -app "${SRCDS_APPID}" \
    -pubfile "${WORKSHOP_ITEM_ID}" \
    -username "${STEAM_USER}" \
    -password "${STEAM_PASS}" \
    -remember-password \
    -validate \
    -dir "${STAGING}"
DD_EXIT=$?

if [[ ${DD_EXIT} -ne 0 ]]; then
    echo "-----------------------------------------"
    echo "DepotDownloader failed (exit ${DD_EXIT}). The server files were NOT installed."
    echo "-----------------------------------------"
    exit 1
fi

## A zero exit is necessary but not sufficient - confirm the file the server refuses
## to boot without actually landed.
if [[ ! -f "${STAGING}/${SENTINEL_REL}" ]]; then
    echo "-----------------------------------------"
    echo "DepotDownloader reported success but the payload is incomplete."
    echo "Missing: ${SENTINEL_REL}"
    echo "Contents of the staging directory:"
    ls -la "${STAGING}"
    echo "-----------------------------------------"
    exit 1
fi

## Move the deployment root into place. BannerlordCoopServer.exe must sit at the root
## of a folder containing engine/ and server-data/, which is how the item ships it.
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installing server files..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"
rm -rf /mnt/server/DedicatedServer
mv -f "${STAGING}/DedicatedServer" /mnt/server/DedicatedServer

## Clean up the staging area and the downloader; the payload is now in place and the
## quota is better spent on saves and logs.
rm -rf "${STAGING}" "${DD_DIR}"

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Steam user
variables.description: Steam account that owns Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord. Required - anonymous login cannot download the Coop Workshop item.

variables.name: App id
variables.description: Base game App ID the Coop Workshop item is registered under.

variables.name: Workshop item id
variables.description: Steam Workshop item id for Bannerlord Coop.

variables.name: WINEDEBUG
variables.description: Silences Wine's own debug/fixme output, which is otherwise very noisy. Don't change this.

variables.name: WINEARCH
variables.description: Forces Wine to create a 64-bit prefix. BannerlordCoopServer.exe is 64-bit; don't change this.

variables.name: Winetricks
variables.description: Packages installed into the wine prefix on boot. BannerlordCoopServer.exe requires a .NET runtime; if the server fails to start with a missing-.NET error, add the appropriate dotnetdesktopNN package here.

variables.name: Server Password
variables.description: Connection password, up to 128 characters. Joining players are prompted for it; blank = no password. Applied to server-config.json at boot by a line-level edit that preserves the file's comments. The server creates that file on its first run, so settings apply from the second start onward.

variables.name: Auto update
variables.description: Leave disabled. This egg installs the Workshop item directly, not the full game - the image's built-in app_update-on-boot only tries (and fails) to install app 261550 against the wrong platform.

variables.name: Save name
variables.description: World/save to host, from the 'Game Saves' folder (no .sav extension). If it does not exist, a fresh world is created from default_new_game.sav under this name. Two previous generations are kept as <name>.backup1 / .backup2.

variables.name: Autosave interval (minutes)
variables.description: Minutes between world autosaves. 0 disables autosaving.

variables.name: Steam advertising
variables.description: 1 = advertise on Steam (public lobby, friend joins, traffic relayed over Steam so no port forwarding is needed) when a logged-in Steam client runs on the host. 0 = direct connect on UDP 4200 only. Defaults to 0: a dedicated container normally has no Steam client running, and enabling this without one hangs the server at boot.

variables.name: Write log file
variables.description: 1 = also write everything the server prints to logs/coop-server-*.log (one file per launch, newest 10 kept). 0 = console only.
